name: Glass Loupe & Refraction
summary: A heavy optical loupe glides over a calm metrics table and reveals the coral anomaly that is invisible outside the glass.
look: Near-white grid paper, dense calm tables and a metal-barrelled loupe with Fresnel rim, caustic light and chromatic fringes. Coral ink exists only under the lens.

components.name: SDF lens
components.role: a circular refraction pass (or a scaled DOM copy) magnifying what sits under it

components.name: Metal barrel
components.role: conic-gradient ring and handle that make it a physical instrument

components.name: Dispersion
components.role: red/cyan channel offset on everything seen through the glass

components.name: Fresnel rim
components.role: bright edge band + faint coral/ink fringe at the lens border

components.name: Hidden ink
components.role: coral marks that only render inside the lens mask — the anomaly

components.name: Hanging tag
components.role: mono readout on a leader line off the loupe: time + deploy

motion.name: Lens glide
motion.how: bezier path, sine.inOut 3 s = 6 beats; each row or card crossing lands on a beat

motion.name: Magnify settle
motion.how: scale 1 → 1.8, expo.out 0.3 s, triggered on a downbeat when the lens stops

motion.name: Dispersion spike
motion.how: RGB split 0 → 8 px → 0 over 3 frames on the snare when the anomaly is found

story: Hook: a loupe glides over 38 calm dashboard thumbnails and finds Friday's missed drop. Reveal: the lens centres on the drop, magnifies and splits the Acme mark, then “Acme Pulse” resolves. Proof: the loupe scans a metrics table; on the checkout row the neutral 3.1% refracts into “−18%” with the tag “since 09:42 · after deploy #2231”, and the human chooses “Roll back”. CTA: “Caught before customers noticed.” with the loupe at rest and “Start free”.
adapt: Lay your product's densest real screen (a log, a list, a table) flat and let the loupe find the one row your product flags; the hidden-ink trick works for any “we noticed this” feature.

references.note: refractive glass over a grid in WebGPU

fit.risk: Real refraction needs WebGL and a pre-baked table texture; the DOM fallback must line up exactly.
